chapters.title: Notifications
intro: This chapter is for everyone who uses the desk. It explains how SupportDesk tells you about new work and urgent events.
It covers the bell, the **Notifications** page, acknowledging critical alerts and desktop alerts.

sections.title: How notifications reach you
sections.intro: SupportDesk notifies you when something needs you. Examples are a new assignment, a customer reply or an SLA breach.

blocks.caption: The bell in the top bar with the number of unread notifications.
blocks.alt: Top bar with the bell highlighted and a red badge showing 99+

rows: A red badge with the number of unread notifications, or 99+ when there are more. The bell shows a ringing icon when an item needs acknowledgement.
Warnings and critical items also appear briefly on the screen.
After you allow them, warnings and critical items also appear on your computer's desktop.
The **Customer replies & mentions** card shows your latest replies and @mentions.
Your administrator decides which events also arrive this way.

blocks.note: New notifications arrive live. You do not need to reload the page.

sections.title: Check your notifications from the bell
sections.intro: The bell panel shows your latest notifications without leaving the page you are on.
steps: In the top bar, select the bell.

steps.text: Read the list. The newest notification is at the top.
steps.caption: The bell panel with critical items that need acknowledgement and unread warnings.
steps.alt: Notifications panel with Mark all read, a desktop alerts prompt and a list of notifications with Acknowledge buttons and unread dots

steps: To open the ticket or page behind a notification, select the notification.
To close the panel without opening anything, press [[Esc]] or select outside the panel.
sections.result: The notification you selected is marked as read, and its page opens. Links to other websites open in a new browser tab.

list: The icon colour shows how urgent the item is. See [Notification colours](#nt-colours).
A blue dot at the right marks an unread item.
**Acknowledge** appears on critical items that need it.
When the list is empty, the panel says **You're all caught up.**

sections.title: Mark notifications as read
sections.intro: Mark items as read when you have seen them, so that new ones stand out.
steps: To mark one item, select the blue dot at its right.
To mark every item, select **Mark all read** at the top of the panel.
sections.result: The items lose their unread mark. The number on the bell goes down.

blocks.note: **Mark all read** skips items that need acknowledgement. They stay unread until you acknowledge them.

blocks.tip: On the **Notifications** page, each unread item has a **Mark read** button.

sections.title: Acknowledge a critical notification
sections.intro: Some critical notifications, such as SLA breaches, need you to confirm that you have seen them. While one waits, the bell shows a ringing icon.
steps: Select the bell, or open the **Notifications** page.
Find the item with the **Acknowledge** button.
Read the item. To see the ticket, select the item.
sections.result: The button disappears. On the **Notifications** page, an **Acknowledged** badge takes its place. The item is also marked as read.

blocks.note: Acknowledging also stops any copies of the alert that are still waiting to go out, such as e-mail or push.

blocks.tip: To see only the items you still need to acknowledge, use the **Needs acknowledgement** filter on the **Notifications** page.

sections.title: The Notifications page
sections.intro: The **Notifications** page shows your latest 200 notifications. To open it, select **View all notifications** at the bottom of the bell panel. You can also run **Go to Notifications** from the command palette.

blocks.caption: The **Notifications** page.
blocks.alt: Notifications page with numbered highlights on Enable desktop alerts, Mark all read, the filter buttons, the type list, a notification and its Acknowledge button

callouts: **Enable desktop alerts**. After you answer, this place shows whether desktop alerts are on or blocked.
**Mark all read** marks every unread item as read, except items that need acknowledgement.
The filters: **All**, **Unread** and **Needs acknowledgement**. Each shows how many items it has.
The type list. Choose a type, such as **SLA breaches**, to show only that type.
A notification: title, details, type, time and an **unread** mark. Select it to open its page.
The actions: **Acknowledge** for critical items, or **Mark read** for unread items.

blocks.note: When nothing matches your filter, the page says **No notifications here**.

sections.title: Filter the notifications list
sections.intro: Filter the list to find what needs your attention first.

steps.text: To show one kind of notification, choose it in the **All types** list.
steps.caption: The list filtered to items that need acknowledgement.
steps.alt: Notifications page with the Needs acknowledgement filter selected and a list of SLA breach items with Acknowledge buttons

steps: To show every type again, choose **All types**.
sections.result: The list shows only the matching notifications. Your filter stays while you are on the page.

sections.title: Notification types
sections.intro: The type list on the **Notifications** page offers only the types you have received.

rows: A ticket is assigned to you.
A customer replies on your ticket.
An SLA target is at risk.
An SLA target is missed. These often need acknowledgement.
A request waits for your decision.
Someone approved or rejected your request.
A follow-up reminder you set is due.
The AI Assistant suggests an action that needs a decision.
SupportDesk finds an unusual spike, such as many tickets about one issue.
A live chat is waiting for an agent.
A chat is transferred to you.
Something in the workspace needs attention, for example a connection to another system was turned off.

sections.title: Notification colours
sections.intro: The icon colour shows how urgent a notification is.

rows: Critical or error, such as an SLA breach.
Warning, such as an SLA at risk or an escalation.
Good news, such as a success.

sections.title: Turn on desktop alerts
sections.intro: Desktop alerts show warnings and critical items even when the desk is in a background tab. Your browser asks for your permission once.
steps: In the box that says **Get desktop alerts for urgent notifications.**, select **Enable**.
sections.result: The box disappears. The **Notifications** page now says **Desktop alerts on for warnings and critical items**.
blocks: You can also select **Enable desktop alerts** on the **Notifications** page or the Command Center.
Select a desktop alert to bring the desk to the front and open the item.

blocks.note: If you select **Block**, the page says **Desktop alerts are blocked in this browser.** To change your answer, open your browser's site settings for SupportDesk.

sections.title: Notification preferences
intro: You cannot change your own notification preferences in the desk yet.
Your administrator sets the defaults for everyone. For each event, they choose in-app, e-mail, push or a digest. They also set quiet hours, when e-mail and push wait until later.

blocks.note: Critical alerts ignore quiet hours. The chapter about notification settings explains the defaults.

troubleshooting.problem: The bell panel says **Notifications could not be loaded.**
troubleshooting.cause: The desk could not fetch your notifications.
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Retry**. If it fails again, check your connection.

troubleshooting.problem: Some notifications stay unread after **Mark all read**.
troubleshooting.cause: Items that need acknowledgement are not marked by **Mark all read**.

troubleshooting.problem: The number on the bell is lower than the **Unread** count on the **Notifications** page.
troubleshooting.cause: The bell counts only the latest notifications in its panel.
troubleshooting.fix: Open the **Notifications** page and use the **Unread** filter.

troubleshooting.problem: A **Could not acknowledge** or **Could not mark all as read** message appears.
troubleshooting.cause: The change did not reach SupportDesk.
troubleshooting.fix: Check your connection, then try again.

troubleshooting.cause: Desktop alerts are not allowed in this browser, or your computer is in a do-not-disturb mode.
troubleshooting.fix: Allow notifications for SupportDesk in your browser's site settings. Check your computer's notification settings too.

faq.q: Can I choose which notifications I get?
faq.a: Not yet. Your administrator sets which events reach you in the app, by e-mail, by push or in a digest.

faq.q: Why does the bell show fewer notifications than the Notifications page?
faq.a: The bell shows only your latest notifications. The **Notifications** page shows the latest 200, with filters.

faq.q: Do I get desktop alerts for every notification?
faq.a: No. Desktop alerts and pop-up messages are only for warnings and critical items.

glossary.definition: A message from SupportDesk about something that needs you, such as an assignment, a customer reply or an SLA breach.
Confirm that you have seen a critical notification. It also stops further copies of that alert.
A notification that your browser shows on your computer's desktop, outside the desk page. You must allow it once.
A single e-mail that collects several notifications, sent hourly or daily.
Hours when SupportDesk holds back e-mail and push notifications. Critical alerts still go out.
